title: Policy-weighted routing caused variant misselection and cross-region oscillation — action items
creator: Lina Morales
description:
Summary: During a capacity pressure window on 2025-11-19 we observed a spike in 5xx errors and elevated tail latency for a subset of hosted API customers. The root trigger was a policy-weighting bug in smart routing that caused an incompatible model variant (low-precision quantized variant) to be selected for requests originating from non-primary regions. The variant selection combined with a region-affinity recalculation race produced repeated cross-region reroutes (oscillation) that amplified load and surfaced as cascading errors in the serving cluster.

Impact: ~4% of global requests experienced an increased error rate for ~27 minutes; affected customers reported truncation/invalid-generation symptoms when the quantized variant was used for workloads requiring fp16 kernels. Latency P95 increased ~300ms for those requests. Internal dashboards showed routing churn and repeated model-stitch events.

Root cause (short): policy-weight computation ignored a minimum compatible-variant-sum safeguard when computing weighted fallback buckets. When region capacity dropped below the threshold, the policy engine picked variants only by weight without validating capability (kernel/quantization compatibility) for the requesting region. A concurrent cache invalidation routine and a probe-rebalance job caused rapid re-evaluation of weights, producing oscillating reroutes between regions until the manual mitigations were applied.

Key technical details: 
- The policy evaluator returns a weighted list of candidate variants; a bug in function computeWeightedCandidates() allowed zero-sum edge cases to return small-weight entries that lacked 'compatibility_tags' for the origin region.
- KV cache TTL for route decisions was 1s during the incident due to an aggressive experiment; short TTL combined with the rebalancer (runs every 800ms) caused route churn.
- The quantized variant lacked a fallback shim for signature-compatibility; in many cases the model executed but returned malformed tokens.

Immediate mitigations performed: 
1) Rolled back the TTL experiment to 10s across affected regions (hotfix deployed 2025-11-19 15:42 UTC).
2) Enabled a temporary routing circuit-breaker that prefers same-region, same-precision variants when health is borderline (toggle: routing.circuit_breaker.same_region_preference = true).
3) Reverted an unrelated routing weight tweak that had lowered minimum weight thresholds (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/7859).
4) Contacted impacted customers and opened support cases; created a short-lived transparency post in status.redwood.ai.

Proposed permanent fixes / action items (owners and target dates): 
- A1: Add compatibility validation step in computeWeightedCandidates() so any candidate without required compatibility_tags is excluded (owner: Ethan Kim, due: 2025-11-30).
- A2: Introduce a min-compatible-weight guard: if total compatible weight < 0.2, fall back to pinned same-region model or fail fast with 429 and explanatory error (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-12-07).
- A3: Rework route TTL experiment infra to disallow TTLs < 5s in production; add feature-flag guard and an experiment safety check (owner: Lina Morales, due: 2025-12-01).
- A4: Add end-to-end test in staging that simulates region capacity drops and verifies variant compatibility and no cross-region oscillation (owner: SRE team lead Marco Alvarez, due: 2025-12-12).
- A5: Add telemetry metric 'routing.variant_compatibility_failures' and an alert: rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers paged incident (owner: Observability - Anya Petrov, due: 2025-11-28).
- A6: Backfill model metadata to ensure every variant advertises precision, kernel-support, and incompatible-model-tags; run audit job to find gaps (owner: Model Onboarding - Jonah Li, due: 2025-12-10).

Verification plan: after A1/A2 deploys, run controlled chaos tests: reduce capacity in us-west region and assert no oscillation and that affected requests either hit compatible variants or return a controlled 429 with helpful remediation. Metrics to watch: reroute_rate, cross_region_reroute_count, variant_compatibility_failures, request_success_ratio.

Artifacts and links: See timeline updates and links below for PRs, dashboards and the incident runbook.
